The '''Forward Defense Doctrine''' was an Astorian military-security doctrine that justified expansion, forward basing, and pressure on neighboring states as necessary for national survival.

== Development ==

By the late 1880s, Astoria used the doctrine to explain its growing military presence along the Bakorian border. Under Lord Commander Ahmet Veil, Astoria framed forward bases and contested territory as defensive necessities rather than acts of aggression.

== Bakorian War ==

The doctrine became the strategic basis for the [[Bakorian War]]. Astorian planners treated eastern Bakoria and [[Azmetan]] as security objectives that would protect Astoria, strengthen logistics, and provide industrial depth.

The victory in 1935 validated the doctrine within Astoria. Outside Astoria, it convinced neighboring states that Astorian security language could be a cover for annexation.
